name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 18, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:02 p.m., on November 18, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 15, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

RECESS

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:05 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Ury returned to the
meeting at 6:10 p.m.

City Council Minutes  1  November 18, 2013
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Reardon presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter"
  Corporal Ian B. Moore and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant Artur
  Shvartsberg.

*Items P2 and P3 were taken out of order.

P3.  Business Recognition - Cal Med Pharmacy

  Mayor Reardon presented a proclamation to the owner of Cal Med Pharmacy, John Bruce
  and his family.

P2.  Business Recognition - Portola Plaza McDonald’s

  Mayor Reardon presented a proclamation to Fred and Fran Hill, owners of the Portola
  Plaza McDonald's.

P4.  Never Ever Give Up (NEGU)/ Jessie Rees Foundation - Help support kids fighting
  cancer by donating items to fill Joy Jars

  Mayor Reardon introduced young Cade Spinello, who is recovering from a brain tumor
  and a stroke. Cade's father Mike discussed Cade's progress and how Joy Jars helped his
  son during treatment.

  Erik Rees discussed the NEGU Joy Jars which were created by his daughter Jessie as she
  battled cancer. Mr. Rees announced that they will be collecting toys for Joy Jars at the
  Santa's arrival celebration and from boxes placed at city facilities.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: discussed his recent request for copies of email correspondence between the
City Manager and other local City Managers regarding himself and the Common Sense
Newspaper. He noted that the City responded that there were no pertinent records on file
however he was able to obtain a copy of email correspondence between the City Manager and
the City Manager of San Juan Capistrano.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: asked why Council Meeting video tapes are not retained indefinitely.

City Council Minutes  2  November 18, 2013
 Marlene Gerloff, M.V.: discussed the progress of public art in Mission Viejo and stated that there
is room to expand.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he has been trying, since June, to get a meeting with the
police chief and he expressed concern with escalating police costs and the amount of unfunded
liability with Sheriff's Department pension costs.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3 and 4 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 21, 2013, as
  presented; and (2) approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of November
  4, 2013, as presented.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2013

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for September 2013

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  September 2013

  Received and filed.
City Council Minutes  3  November 18, 2013
 8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for September 2013

  Received and filed.

9.  Amend Library Hours for 2014 Calendar Year

  Approved closure of the Library from Tuesday, December 23 - Sunday, December 28,
  2014. Remain open on MLK Day, January 20, Presidents Day, February 17 and Veterans
  Day, November 11, 2014. The total number of hours the library is open to the public
  throughout the year will remain the same.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated October 25, 2013 in the Amount of $1,929,881.93

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment to Alliant Services Inc. for liability
  insurance for the ITF Wheelchair Tennis Masters event and whether or not the International
  Tennis Federation (ITF) would be reimbursing the City.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas confirmed that the City's contract with the
  ITF included reimbursement for the cost of insurance.

4.  Check Register Dated November 1, 2013 in the Amount of $1,997,769.48

  Council Member Schlicht asked if the day porter at city hall is a new position.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that it is not a
  new position.

Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to ratify the
accompanying check registers for agenda items 3 and 4.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

City Council Minutes  4  November 18, 2013
 STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

18. Amendment to the Orange County Fire Authority Joint Powers Authority Agreement
  Related to the Equity Issue

  Division Chief Kirk Wells introduced OCFA Assistant Chief of Business Services Lori
  Zeller who presented information on the equity issue. Chief Wells and Assistant Chief
  Zeller answered questions of the City Council.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that Mission Viejo needs to do its own cost study and he
  believes that Mission Viejo is overpaying OCFA for fire services.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to (1)
  receive the OCFA presentation; (2) approve the Second Amendment to the Amended
  Orange County Fire Authority JPA Agreement; and (3) authorize the City Attorney to join
  in supporting the OCFA's validation action, when filed, seeking to obtain a judicial
  declaration of the validity of the Second Amendment to the Amended JPA Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:37 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
8:52 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley returned to the dais
at 8:53 p.m.

OLD BUSINESS

10. Agreement to Purchase Replacement to City’s Financial Management Software

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander presented the staff report and
  answered the City Council Member's questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to (1)
  approve 5-year agreement with Tyler Technologies, Inc. for the acquisition,
  implementation and ongoing support of the Munis Financial Management System and issue
  purchase orders under this agreement in an amount not to exceed $676,524; and (2)

City Council Minutes  5  November 18, 2013
   approve 3 agreements with Go Live Technology, Inc. and issue purchase orders under these
  agreements in amounts not to exceed $231,998 for project management services, not to
  exceed $30,000 for data integration services, and not to exceed $30,000 for data conversion
  services; and (3) authorize the City Manager to execute amendments to the Tyler
  Technologies, Inc. and Go Live Technology Inc. agreements in an amount not to exceed
  10% of the total contracts.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

11. Community Services Funding Program - Funding for Fiscal Year 2013-2014

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Mayor Reardon announced that she received an email from an individual who asked about
  a Commissioner's role with one of the organizations that requested money from the City.

  Council Member Schlicht read a prepared statement regarding a Community Services
  Commissioner's involvement with an organization which was not disclosed until after the
  Commissioner was asked about it.

  Council Member Schlicht noted that some of the agencies requesting funding from the City
  have also requested use of City facilities and she is not supportive of free use of space. She
  expressed concern that without local access, an agency would be unable to serve Mission
  Viejo's citizens and that our dollars will be used to fund programs in other areas.

  Mayor Reardon announced that she is a PAL member of the Assistance League of
  Saddleback Valley and she would therefore recuse herself from the vote on that particular
  funding request.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
  Community Services Commission's recommended funding amounts for Fiscal Year 2013-
  2014 for the Community Services Funding Program with the exception of funding for the
  Assistance League of Saddleback Valley.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  6  November 18, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Reardon departed the room and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley assumed the role of Chair.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve
  the Community Services Commission’s recommended funding for the Assistance League
  of Saddleback Valley.

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Reardon

  Mayor Reardon returned to the meeting.

12. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he is surprised that OCFA Assistant Chief Lori
  Zeller doesn't know the total amount of OCFA's unfunded liability. He also noted that John
  Wayne airport was in the process of privatizing fire services and he asked why OCFA
  needs a judge to approve the 2nd amendment to the JPA agreement. Lastly, Mr.
  Wontrobski stated that OCFA should supply him and the City Council with the total labor
  costs for Mission Viejo's three fire stations for the last three years.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

13. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

14. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

15. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

16. SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

City Council Minutes  7  November 18, 2013
   Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

17. Orange County Vector Control District

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that there is a huge overpopulation of crows at the Home
  Depot center and he asked Council Member Leckness to get involved with the problem.

  Council Member Leckness presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg thanked the Council Members for recognizing IT Director Jackie
Alexander for her negotiation skills with the financial system software purchase. He also thanked
Director Dyas for her due diligence and hard work with the financial system evaluation process.

Mr. Wilberg further recognized Steve Bell and Jason Harnett for organizing the staff team that
planned the Wheelchair Tennis Masters and he acknowledged that all of the staff efforts made it
a very successful event.

Council Member Schlicht asked if the ITF has reimbursed the City for expenditures related to the
Wheelchair Masters. She also expressed concern that the ITF is listing Mission Viejo as the host
city for next year's event on their website.

City Manager Wilberg responded that there is an option in the contract that would allow for
renewal and hosting again next year. That matter will come back to the City Council for
consideration at a later date.

City Attorney’s Report

Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with item number 9 in the conditions of approval
for the Kaleidoscope signage plan.

Mr. Curley responded that the City can regulate time, place and manner rather than content.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

City Council Minutes  8  November 18, 2013
 Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness commended staff for hosting the International Wheelchair Tennis
Masters events. He thanked Steve Bell and Jason Harnett for bringing the idea forward and he
commended the City Manager for saying yes and taking it on. The décor was phenomenal, the
spectator stands were great and it was just an inspiring experience for everyone. Council
Member Leckness stated that Mission Viejo made the athletes feel special and he hopes that the
City will host the event again next year.

Council Member Schlicht

20. Farmers Market

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the Farmers Market is failing and she doesn't think
  that the City should continue with it. She further stated that the City's taxpayers should not
  support a private enterprise.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay agreed that the Farmers
  Market seems to have run its course and he has notified the vendor that the City will
  consider discontinuing the market or reinventing it after the first of the year.

Council Member Schlicht announced that her vote against the OCFA equity agreement (agenda
item 18) was based on her belief that it is basically a redistribution of the wealth and that OCFA
chose cities with small populations to win their vote since the votes were not weighted. She
stated that she is anxious to see what the County does next month and she hopes that they will
realize the fallacy of it and vote no. She also expressed concern that the City's General Fund is
taking tax dollars and she stated there should be a way to reimburse taxpayers for the monies
they have paid towards fire services. Council Member Schlicht announced that Saddleback
College will host the football Beach Bowl game on Saturday, November 23 at 5:00 p.m. at the
Saddleback campus. She noted that local football is always fun and she enjoyed the last
Diablos game which was another Mission Viejo blowout. She also attended the City's solemn
Veterans Day ceremony and it was standing room only. She stated that it was a beautiful event
and she expressed thanks and appreciation to all of the veterans and their families. Council
Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at a recent San Juan Capistrano City Council Meeting
and the American Legion Pancake breakfast where she won a raffle prize. She announced that
the Saddleback Republican Assembly meets on Thursday, November 21 with guest speaker Ken
Maddox who will discuss the problems in government and the Diablos football team will take
on Mater Dei High School on November 22. She concluded by wishing everyone a happy
Chanukah, a happy Thanksgiving and she read the following quote from Thomas Jefferson:
"The democracy will cease to exist when you take away from those who are willing to work and
give to those who would not."

City Council Minutes  9  November 18, 2013
  Council Member Ury

 Council Member Ury stated that the Wheelchair Masters tennis tournament was a lot of fun and
 it showed what an incredible amount of perseverance that certain people have to go
 through. Once again it gave him perspective that no matter what we have to deal with; there are
 always people who have it rougher than we do. Council Member Ury thanked staff for a great
 job and he commended the athletes on the incredible tennis that he saw them play. He also
 thanked staff for a great job on the Veterans Day ceremony. It was exciting for him to be able
 to introduce the Veterans of the Year and it was an honor to be there and see the people who
 didn't wait for the United States to call and ask them to step up, they stepped up on their
 own. Council Member Ury expressed his hope that this generation will pass on to its kids, the
 understanding and appreciation for the kind of sacrifices that our service men and women make.

 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley commented on the Veterans Day event and she agreed that it seems to
 get bigger and better every year. She noted that staff did a great job and it is really nice to take
 one day out of the year to honor our veterans. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, along with Mayor
 Reardon, also attended the Veterans Day event at El Toro Memorial Park and she stated that it
 was very nice as well. She further agreed with her colleagues that the Wheelchair Tennis
 Masters were outstanding and she couldn't help but think about the beautiful new tennis center
 that the City consciously decided to invest-in and to modernize. Right after the facility was
 made more functional, Mission Viejo became the 1st city in the United States to host the
 International Wheelchair Tennis Masters and it was just very impressive. She stated that some
 people worried that we might be in over our heads but City staff was so well prepared and she
 thanked Steve Bell, Brian Gruner, Jason Harnett and the army of volunteers and staff members
 who worked at the event. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley said that she is looking forward to using
 pictures from the Masters for the City's character program posters which will depict
 perseverance and unity. She also outlined her attendance, on behalf of Mayor Reardon, at the
 City Selection meeting where she was very pleased to see Council Member Ury win the vote to
 serve on the OCTA Board of Directors again. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley congratulated Council
 Member Ury and stated that he has done a really excellent job in representing the City and also
 the region and she noted that he won his reappointment by a great margin.

 Mayor Reardon

 Mayor Reardon agreed with her colleague's comments on the wheelchair tennis event. She
 noted that photographer Steve Wylie took over 10,000 pictures and she encouraged everyone to
 view the photos at www.stevewyliephotography.com. She took her young grandson to watch
 the tennis one evening and the boy was overwhelmed by how hard the athletes hit the ball from
 a wheelchair. She said that she talked with many of the players and coaches and they had
 nothing but compliments for the City and staff. Mayor Reardon also noted that the tennis center
 building and the seating areas with the artificial turf benches were great, and the whole facility
 was just so welcoming and inviting. She complimented the volunteers and she observed that
 tennis center members were also helping out each day. Mayor Reardon stated that it was just
City Council Minutes  10  November 18, 2013
  phenomenal and life altering to watch these superb athletes who are fierce competitors and she
 announced that tournament director Steve Bell and wheelchair tennis founder Brad Parks will
 be coming to the next meeting to thank the City Council for agreeing to host the event. She also
 discussed her attendance at the City's Veterans Day ceremony which was very well attended and
 so full of meaning and significance. In addition, she attended the El Toro Memorial Park
 service as well as Veterans Day events at the Elks Club, Casta del Sol and Saddleback
 College. At the college, veterans talked about how meaningful the veterans’ memorial is to
 them and one vet discussed how he never waned to go to school but after joining the Marines,
 he is now in college and making a 4.0 GPA. Mayor Reardon concluded her comments by
 thanking staff for all of their efforts with the City's events.

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 10:38 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
 session, Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting to Monday, December 2, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________________
 Karen Hamman, City Clerk

 Approved at the meeting of December 2, 2013

City Council Minutes  11  November 18, 2013
